Problem: Chen says: “Don't be afraid of temporary difficulties and setbacks. 不经历风雨怎么见彩虹?” Child retorts: “You are wrong. I have experienced so much wind and rain, how come I haven't seen a rainbow?” Which item is child's answer most suitable to rebut?
Options:
A. Even if experienced wind and rain, may not see rainbow.
B. If experience wind and rain, then can see rainbow.
C. Only if experience wind and rain, can see rainbow.
D. If want see rainbow, must experience wind and rain.

We need identify logical form of father's rhetorical question. "不经历风雨怎么见彩虹?" Usually means "If not experience wind/rain, cannot see rainbow" i.e. 只有经历风雨，才能见彩虹 / 必须经历风雨才能见彩虹. That's necessary condition: see rainbow -> experience wind/rain. Equivalent contrapositive: not experience -> not see. It does NOT imply sufficient condition: experience -> see. Child says experienced but no rainbow, which refutes sufficient condition "if experience then see" (B). It is consistent with necessary condition: experience necessary but not sufficient. So answer B.

Check wording: "最适宜用来反驳以下哪项" child's counterexample: P (experience) true, Q (see rainbow) false. Refutes P -> Q. Option B: 只要经历了风雨，就可以见到彩虹. In Chinese "只要...就..." sufficient condition: If P then Q. A says even if P, may not Q, which supports child, not refuted by child? Actually child's answer is evidence against B. D: If want Q, must P = necessary, same as C roughly? "只有P才Q" = Q->P, not refuted by P true Q false. D = Q->P too. So B.

Need final with explanation concise and final line 答案：B. Ensure format exactly. Final line no quotes.
content:
陈先生孩子举出的反例是“经历了风雨，但没见到彩虹”。这能反驳的是“只要经历风雨，就一定能见到彩虹”这种充分条件判断；而不能反驳“必须经历风雨才可能见到彩虹”这种必要条件判断。

答案：B
